title: Go: Multi-Level Cache
description: Build a multi-level caching system in Go with LRU eviction, TTL expiration, write-through strategy, and cache statistics.

steps.title: LRU eviction with container/list
steps.description: Implement an LRU cache using `container/list` for ordering and `map[string]*list.Element` for O(1) lookups. Implement `Get(key)` and `Set(key, value)` with eviction of the least recently used item when over capacity. Print cache state after each operation.
hints: Each list element stores a `KeyValue` struct with key and value
On `Get`, move the accessed element to the front with `l.MoveToFront(el)`
On `Set` when full, evict the back element with `l.Remove(l.Back())`

verification.successMessage: LRU cache with container/list correctly evicts the least recently used item!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'evicted: <key>' when an item is evicted due to capacity.

steps.title: TTL expiration with time.Timer
steps.description: Extend the cache with TTL (time-to-live) support. Each entry stores an expiration timestamp. `Get` checks if the entry is expired and returns `nil, false` if so. Clean up expired entries periodically using `time.Ticker`. Print "Expired: <key>" when entries are cleaned up.
hints: Add an `expiresAt time.Time` field to the cache entry struct
In `Get`, compare `time.Now()` with `expiresAt` before returning the value
Start a background goroutine with `time.NewTicker(5 * time.Second)` for periodic cleanup

verification.successMessage: TTL expiration correctly invalidates and cleans up expired cache entries!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Expired: <key>' when a TTL-expired entry is cleaned up.

steps.title: Write-through strategy
steps.description: Implement a write-through cache strategy. The cache wraps a backing store (a simple map). On `Set`, write to both cache and backing store. On `Get`, check cache first, then backing store on miss, populating the cache. Print "Cache hit", "Cache miss", and "Write through" messages.
hints: Define a `Store` interface with `Get(key)`, `Set(key, value)` for the backing store
The write-through cache implements the same interface and delegates to the store
Print 'Cache miss — fetching from store' when falling through to the backing store

verification.test: output.includes('Cache hit') && output.includes('Cache miss') && output.includes('Write through')
verification.successMessage: Write-through cache correctly coordinates between cache and backing store!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Cache hit', 'Cache miss', and 'Write through' for each operation type.

steps.title: Multi-level cache (L1/L2)
steps.description: Build a `MultiLevelCache` with L1 (fast, small, short TTL) and L2 (slower, larger, longer TTL). On `Get`, check L1 first, then L2 on miss, promoting to L1. On `Set`, write to both. Use `sync.RWMutex` for thread safety. Print which level served each request.
hints: Embed both caches in a struct: `L1 *LRUCache`, `L2 *LRUCache` with different configs
L1 should have a smaller capacity and shorter TTL than L2
Print 'L1 hit' or 'L2 hit' to show which cache level served the request

verification.successMessage: Multi-level cache correctly promotes entries from L2 to L1 on access!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'L1 hit' or 'L2 hit' for each cache request.

steps.title: Cache statistics
steps.description: Add comprehensive stats tracking: hits, misses, evictions, stale reads, average access time. Use `sync/atomic` for counters. Implement a `Stats()` method that returns a struct and a `PrintStats()` method. Run a workout of operations and print the stats report.
hints: Use `time.Since(start)` to measure access times and compute running average
Print a formatted report: `fmt.Printf("Hits: %d, Misses: %d, Hit ratio: %.2f%%\n", ...)`

verification.successMessage: Cache stats accurately report hits, misses, evictions, and hit ratio!
verification.failureMessage: Print a formatted stats report showing hits, misses, evictions, and hit ratio.
